title: Harness doctor forbidden-path rule repair
objective: Repair the existing Harness doctor false positive with the narrowest auditable forbidden-path rule. In harness/config/project.json, modify only forbidden_repository_patterns; active_stage, active_chains, blocked_chains, rule_versions, quality_commands, and future_stage_gate must remain byte-for-byte equivalent to the baseline. Add tests proving those fields do not change, preserve synthetic raw/private wallet-like rejection, and distinguish only documented scrubbed public fixture/aggregate artifacts. Do not silently waive the doctor gate.
forbidden_actions: Do not execute real trades, sign transactions, broadcast transactions, or connect a trading wallet.
Do not read seed phrases, private keys, browser cookies, login sessions, DPAPI material, or trading API keys.
Do not automate a logged-in GMGN page; only consume user-provided offline exports from the private root.
Do not commit wallet addresses, transaction hashes, raw GMGN exports, chainfm_out contents, or private manifests containing raw records.
Do not treat null, unknown, or missing values as zero.
Do not create a cross-chain global wallet score or assume SOL and BSC addresses identify the same entity.
Do not squash, rebase, rewrite pushed history, push to main, or merge a PR.
Within harness/config/project.json, do not modify any field except forbidden_repository_patterns.
Do not change active_stage, active_chains, blocked_chains, rule_versions, quality_commands, or future_stage_gate.
Do not allowlist arbitrary directories or wildcard names without narrowly tested scrubbed-artifact justification.
Do not simply remove wallet*.json or disable the forbidden-file check.
Do not rename or delete existing evidence files merely to hide the failure.
Do not modify product source, provider behavior, runtime credential handling, chain configuration, or package scripts.
